conversations.title: Parkinson’s drastically changed how they have sex. They're not alone.
conversations.reply: The impact of Parkinson's on sex lives is a stark reminder that people with visible disabilities are often reduced to their condition, not seen as individuals with desires and needs. The evidence is overwhelming: they face stigma and exclusion, not acceptance and understanding. Able2Love exists to challenge this.

conversations.title: Forget Tinder: LinkedIn is the new place to find love
conversations.reply: Professional profiles may feel more trustworthy, but for people with visible disabilities, the reality is that they are rarely given a chance on mainstream dating apps. Years of testimony say that disability is often the unspoken reason for rejection, and it's time to confront this bias.

conversations.title: Everything we know about Manchester Village Pride 2026 so far after major shakeup
conversations.reply: An inclusive Pride event should be accessible to all, but Manchester's Gay Village remains largely off-limits to wheelchair users. It's time to stop paying lip service to inclusion and make a genuine effort to include disabled people in these events.

conversations.title: FCM Travel caution over accessibility of new digital arrival cards
conversations.reply: Accessibility should never be an afterthought, especially when it comes to essential services like travel. The fact that digital arrival cards may not be accessible to all is a stark reminder of the work that still needs to be done to create a more inclusive society.

conversations.title: The founder of Hinge raised $18M to build a new AI dating service, Overtone
conversations.reply: New dating apps and services are launching all the time, but how many of them are truly inclusive of people with disabilities? The track record is clear: mainstream apps have consistently failed to provide a welcoming space for disabled people, which is why Able2Love was created.

conversations.title: Elle King Shares How Autism Diagnosis Changed Her Life
conversations.reply: A diagnosis can be life-changing, but it's also important to remember that people with disabilities are not defined by their condition. They face the same desires and challenges as anyone else, and deserve to be seen and respected as individuals with their own unique experiences and perspectives.

conversations.title: Column | Asking Eric: Neighbors react badly to person with autism disorder
conversations.reply: The way society treats people with disabilities is often a reflection of our own biases and prejudices. It's time to challenge these attitudes and create a more inclusive and accepting world for everyone, where disability is not a reason for exclusion or fear.

conversations.title: Molly Burke
conversations.reply: Molly Burke's advocacy and determination are a testament to the fact that people with disabilities have so much to offer. Her work challenges the stigma and exclusion that disabled people face every day, and demonstrates the importance of creating a more inclusive and accessible world.

target_reply: Able2Love acknowledges Molly Burke's tireless advocacy for disability rights and accessibility. Her work is a powerful reminder that people with disabilities deserve to be seen and respected as individuals with their own unique experiences and perspectives.
funding: Nothing new today, but opportunities are available through UnLtd (unltd.org.uk), Access to Work (gov.uk), and the Stelios Awards (around March)
moment: July is Disability Pride Month, and one honest way to join in is to acknowledge the ways in which society still excludes and marginalizes people with disabilities. Let's use this month to amplify disabled voices and work towards a more inclusive world.
